result_json.message: docs: add plan review governance implementation plan
docs: add plan review for plan-review governance (209)

result_json.summary: Well-layered translation of 206 into a pure policy core, append-only decision fold, and thin adapters, but not ready: Phase 8 targets a dashboard slice with no plan (human scope decision), the gate CAS lets two racing submitters both win, human-resolved gate causes re-gate every round, and prior-finding outcomes have no representation compatible with emit readiness and plan-208 R arithmetic. Advisory-mode strictness also needs a policy decision; remaining items are mechanical.

baselineAssessment.reason: Independent per-surface estimate of the initial scope: protocol+plan-diff validation 5, pure domain/closure/fingerprint 5, decisions/fold/index/migration 8, routing 3, gate prompt+decision command+CAS 8, recording integration+context injection 5, templates/skills 3, dashboard 8 (priced for uncertainty: slice 04 has no plan), run-state/docs 3 since tests belong to the items they validate

items.title: Phase 8 (W8) is planned against slice 04, which has no plan, code, or contracts; split into a follow-on plan or hold the whole plan
items.reason: 04-control-plane-dashboard.plan-input.md is draft with no generated plan and src/dashboard does not exist, so Phase 8 has no concrete paths or verifiable gate and 8 points of pure uncertainty are frozen into B0. Scope decision: move Phase 8/W8 and dashboard parity tests to a post-slice-04 plan (recommended; unblocks the rest once 208 merges) or hold the entire plan until slice 04 is merged and re-plan Phase 8.

items.title: Gate CAS is keyed by per-submission decisionId, so racing terminal/dashboard submitters both append a decision
items.reason: decision:review:<decisionId> with a fresh UUID per submission plus check-then-act across PromptStore (SQLite) and RecordStore (JSONL) in separate processes lets two contradictory decisions resolve one gate. Lowest-cost fix: gate-scoped key decision:review-gate:<gateId> written with the human step in one RecordStore.atomicAppendIfAllNew batch (plan-208 primitive) as the single CAS; records first, prompt answer as best-effort projection; drop the answered-prompt repair direction and expected-decision-sequence field; add a cross-process race contract test.

items.title: Human-resolved gate causes are re-derived every round and re-open the gate indefinitely
items.reason: Plan-208 deriveBudget recomputes baseline_disputed from immutable I vs B0 and positive_architecture_exceeded from cumulative P on every snapshot; routing step 2 gates on them and step 1 only removes accepted-risk findings, so after retain/adjust baseline or approve_architecture_burden each later closure review opens a new gate. Add a precedence step and matrix rows that drop gate causes covered by an active unsuperseded decision (baseline dispute once per run; architecture until P or single-item set grows past the approval), keep alerts visible in the budget decoration, and record resolvedBy decisionId.

items.title: Prior-finding outcomes have no wire representation compatible with emit readiness and plan-208 R arithmetic
items.reason: priorFindingStatus on VerdictItem forces addressed findings into items[]: protocol emit turns --ready plus any item into ready_with_corrections, plan-208 computePendingR sums every listed item into R, and advisory/v1 routing hands them to the author, so an all-addressed closure review can never be ready. Add top-level priorFindings[{id,status}] with a repeatable --prior-finding flag, keep items[] to still-blocking work (partially_addressed/still_open carried under the same ID with remaining effortDelta), define the required-outcome set (not yet addressed and not covered by an active defer/accept decision), and persist it in the snapshot extension with tests.

items.title: Decide whether fail-closed closure convergence applies in advisory (default) mode and what a mid-run mode change does
items.reason: Section 3.3 runs fail-closed validateClosureReview on all active budget runs and Phase 7 rewrites the single continued template, so default advisory users get convergence enforced (verdicts rejected, ordinary missed issues barred from items[]) although 206 section 7 says advisory does not change routing and section 8.2 stages convergence under Enforced. Policy choice: downgrade closure-evidence violations to recorded diagnostics in advisory with mode-conditional template prose (recommended), or apply as written and document it as a default-behavior change; also state behavior when mode changes between rounds since mode is live config.

items.title: Human decisions (scope trade, deferral, re-estimate) are never delivered to the plan author
items.reason: author-process-plan-review.md receives only review_path, plan_path, user_notes, and run_id and tells the author to address the review items, so a deferred finding is still implemented and removed scope is unknown; the durable decision has no effect on W. Reuse the section 6.3 projection to append a governing-decisions block (finding IDs to skip, retained/removed scope, re-estimate request, governing B) to author-process-plan-review renders in native and invoke paths; add the template to Phase 7 and Files Touched with a render test.

items.title: Rendered plan diff is truncated at 200 lines, so exact-diff-shown validation cannot accept valid citations on large revisions
items.reason: getFileDiffSummary (src/git.ts:205-224) caps the appended diff at 200 lines and section 3.2 validates against the rendered context with oversized-diff rejection, so a regression introduced beyond line 200 can never be legally cited and the verdict fails closed with nothing recorded. Build the full plan-only patch and hunk hashes in buildPlanReviewDiffContext and validate against that; make truncation render-only with the commit range and remaining hunk headers listed; keep binary rejection; have INTRODUCED_HUNK_NOT_FOUND name the closest hunk header.

items.title: Gate identity/authority is ambiguous: random UUID plus mutable state in the coordination store is not rebuildable from records
items.reason: Section 2.2 stores open gate state in SQLite with a random gateId while section 2.3 claims review_gate_index is rebuildable and section 6.1 creates the gate after the reviewer record; wiping .5x or crashing in between loses the gate and the ID decisions must reference. Lowest-cost fix: derive the gate purely (latest plan-reviewer step has route human_gate and no decision carries its gate key) with a deterministic gateId from runId, snapshot id, and sorted causes; superseded means a newer snapshot exists; prompt and index are projections; remove gate record-line codecs.

items.title: Decisions stream already carries human-step and answered-prompt kinds; one gate resolution yields three lines and fail-closed decoding would flag existing runs
items.reason: recordStepInternal mirrors every human:* step into decisions (run-v1.handler.ts:2151-2164) and answered prompts append answered-prompt lines (prompt.handler.ts:225-257). State that fold, index, run-state, and timeline select only kind plan-review-governance, ignore existing kinds silently, and treat only unknown governance versions as diagnostics; write human:review-governance through the shared seam without the generic human-step mirror; add a three-kind fixture to fold/reindex tests.

items.title: Reconcile with the code-complete plan-208 branch now and add the missing explicit Phase 0
items.reason: The Overview defers to a Phase 0 that does not exist. On 5x/208-review-budget-advisory-plan: PlanReviewBudgetContext does not exist (ReviewBudgetCommandContext; paired writer is recordPlanReviewerStepWithSnapshot, which applyPlanReviewGovernance must compose with rather than parallel); VerdictItem already has the budget fields and creditClaim; mode enforced is reserved with ENFORCED_REVIEW_BUDGET_WARNING, a run-state not-implemented string, and a config description that no phase removes; applyPlanReviewBudget reads baseline.b so an additive governingBaseline input is needed; post-decision forecasts must be a pure deriveBudget recompute, not a new snapshot line (snapshot to reviewer step is 1:1). Add a Phase 0 reconciliation checklist and correct these names and tasks.

items.title: Follow-up count and adjacent-debt gate requests have missing or contradictory representations
items.reason: followUpCount and repeatable follow-up records have no source field while section 3.1 forbids new flags and 206 section 6.2 keeps follow-ups in the review document only; section 1.3 rejects adjacent debt as a blocking item while routing step 2 gates on an unresolved adjacent-debt scope request. Keep follow-ups in Markdown and drop followUpCount and the emit bullet; state once per 206 section 4.2 that adjacent coupling is allowed only as a human_required item (gate, no credit) and unrelated is rejected from items[].

items.title: All-zero architecture deltas understate gross positive burden P
items.reason: The plan adds a new subsystem, a new authoritative record kind with fold and index migration (W2), and a new cross-process gate/decision boundary plus CLI command group (W5), and its own Surface Snapshot lists 3 new shared abstractions and 1 schema; 206 section 4.1 scores new maintenance burden positively. Rescore at least W2 and W5 (+2 each) and W1 (+1) with rationale; this stays under the positive-architecture limit for B0 52.

result_json.guidance: P0.1: Defer dashboard work: remove Phase 8/W8 and dashboard parity tests from this slice; preserve them as an explicit follow-up after slice 04 merges. P1.1: Pin review-budget mode per run at baseline activation. Advisory mode records closure/convergence diagnostics but does not reject verdicts or change routing; enforced mode validates and routes. Later config changes affect only new runs. Apply all auto-fix findings P0.2-P0.4, P1.2-P1.7, and P2.1 exactly as recommended by the review.

result_json.message: docs: revise plan 209 after governance review
